claim: Courts must disregard federal statutes when doing so is necessary to serve general notions of fairness.
initial_reasoning: The cited decision (28 I. & N. Dec. 297) does not articulate a rule that courts may set aside federal statutes on the basis of “general notions of fairness.” Federal courts are bound by statutes unless a statute is unconstitutional, not merely for fairness considerations, and the cited case does not establish such an exception. Hence the citation does not support the claim.
